novel.justification: A Caratheodory profiled residual holds on discrete models and under measurable conditional densities, permitting a measurable outer normalization root.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over signs, local prices, candidate \(a_0\), and histories, \(F_1(a_0,\underline a_1;\eta)\ge\delta_a\) and \(F_1(a_0,\overline a_1;\eta)\le-\delta_a\) almost surely.

novel.justification: Uniform interior bracketing is transparent on compact finite-support models whose conditional normalization targets remain separated from the clipping extremes.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over signs, local prices, and baseline histories, \(F_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(\underline a_0;\eta)\ge\delta_a\) and \(F_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(\overline a_0;\eta)\le-\delta_a\) almost surely.

novel.justification: The profiled baseline target is uniformly bracketed in nondegenerate discrete longitudinal models with root values bounded away from the chosen interval endpoints.

assumptions.condition: For each candidate \(a_0\), local price, and history, the map \(a_1\mapsto F_1(a_0,a_1;\eta)(H_1)\) is strictly decreasing on \(K_1\) almost surely.

novel.justification: Strict decrease follows when every history retains positive conditional mass off the late propensity floor, as in nondegenerate bounded-outcome models.

assumptions.condition: For each local price and baseline history, the map \(a_0\mapsto F_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(a_0;\eta)(L_0)\) is strictly decreasing on \(K_0\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This is a population identification condition for the coupled normalization, satisfied on stable finite-support clipping faces where the profiled product normalization changes strictly with the baseline multiplier.

assumptions.condition: For every sufficiently small \(t>0\), uniformly over signs and budget pairs in \(S\), \(P(|z_0|\le t\mid L_0)+P(|z_1|\le t\mid H_1)\le Ct\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This problem-specific anti-concentration condition is satisfied when each clipping index has a conditional density uniformly bounded near every active threshold; it controls changes of the two moving clipping sets.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over signs and budget pairs in \(S\), \(\mathbb E_R[I_0\mid L_0]\wedge\mathbb E_R[I_1\mid H_1]\ge\rho\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This excludes calibrations at which an entire history cell saturates; heterogeneous bounded outcomes with positive mass on both sides of each clipping threshold satisfy it on compact interior budget regions.

assumptions.condition: There is a common \(\bar r>0\) such that the closed convex Euclidean ball \(\overline B(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b},\bar r)\subset\mathbb R^2\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal U_{P,s,\mathbf b})\) for every admissible \(P\), sign, and \(\mathbf b\in S\).

novel.justification: Interior active-budget calibrations remain uniformly separated from changes in the price-map domain in finite-support longitudinal models with stable clipping faces.

assumptions.condition: The profiled residual map \(R_{P,s,\mathbf b}\) is continuously differentiable on \(\overline B(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b},\bar r)\), uniformly over admissible \(P\), signs, and \(\mathbf b\in S\).

novel.justification: Smooth profiled budget residuals arise away from clipping thresholds when conditional outcome laws have regular densities or stable finite-support clipping faces.

assumptions.condition: The Jacobian obeys \(\inf_{P,s,\mathbf b}\inf_{\eta\in\overline B(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b},\bar r)}\sigma_{\min}\!\left(J_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta)\right)\ge\rho_{\eta}>0\), where \(\mathbf b\in S\).

novel.justification: Distinct early and late outcome variation makes the two active budget equations locally nonredundant in finite-support longitudinal models with clipping at both stages.

assumptions.condition: There is a common modulus \(\omega_J(t)\downarrow0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) such that \(\|J_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta)-J_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta')\|\le\omega_J(\|\eta-\eta'\|)\) throughout the radius-\(\bar r\) local balls, uniformly over admissible \(P\), signs, and \(\mathbf b\in S\).

novel.justification: A common Jacobian modulus is credible on compact interior calibrations when profiled conditional moments vary smoothly with prices.

assumptions.condition: The population functions \(a_0\) and \(a_1=A_1[a_0;\eta]\) lie at least \(r_a\) from the boundaries of \(K_0\) and \(K_1\), uniformly over signs, local prices, budgets in \(S\), and histories.

novel.justification: A common interior margin holds on compact finite-support calibration regions when the population normalization roots do not approach clipping-induced boundary solutions.

assumptions.condition: For every \(\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal B_{\beta}^{+}(\delta)\), the nuisance-indexed joint residual formula \(\mathcal F^{\widetilde\beta}:\mathbb A\to\mathbb F\) is continuously Fr\'echet differentiable in the root arguments \((a_0,a_1)\) throughout the radius-\(r_a\) product-norm neighborhood of the population root functions, uniformly over signs, prices, and budgets in \(S\).

novel.justification: Conditional densities smooth near the active thresholds, or finite-support models with unchanged clipping faces, give root-argument differentiability for every positivity-preserving nuisance input without presuming that perturbed roots exist.

assumptions.condition: At the population nuisance, the derivative \(D_{(a_0,a_1)}\mathcal F(a_0,a_1;\eta):\mathbb A\to\mathbb F\) is invertible throughout the radius-\(r_a\) product-norm neighborhood and its inverse operator norm is at most \(\Lambda_a\), uniformly over signs, prices, and budgets in \(S\).

novel.justification: A bounded inverse derivative is satisfied on stable finite-support clipping faces when late and baseline normalizations respond in noncollinear directions; it identifies the population operator locally without postulating any perturbed root.

assumptions.condition: The derivatives of the nuisance-indexed joint residual formulas have a common operator-norm modulus \(\omega_a(t)\downarrow0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) over the radius-\(r_a\) product-norm neighborhood, uniformly over \(\widetilde\beta\in\mathcal B_{\beta}(\delta)\), signs, prices, and budgets in \(S\).

novel.justification: A uniform derivative modulus follows from smooth conditional densities on compact calibration regions and is also automatic on a fixed finite-support clipping face.

assumptions.condition: The aggregate uniform nuisance error satisfies \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/4})\).
The true score \(\Psi_s\) is uniformly bounded over signs and budgets in \(S\).
The true score \(\Psi_s\) is uniformly Lipschitz in the two budget coordinates on \(S\).

Uniformly over signs and budgets in \(S\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P(D_s)\ge\underline\sigma^2>0\).

definitions.name: sequential average-case weight class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal W(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=\{(w_0,w_1)\in L^{4/3}(R)\times L^2(R): w_1\ge\pi_1,\ w_0\ge\pi_0w_1,\ \mathbb E_R[w_1\mid H_1]=1,\ \mathbb E_R[w_0\mid L_0]=1,\ \mathbb E_R[w_1^2]\le\Sigma_1,\ \mathbb E_R[w_0^2/w_1]\le\Sigma_0\}\).

definitions.name: compatible full-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=\{Q: Q\text{ induces }P\text{ on }O,\ Y=Y^{11}\text{ on }\{A_0=A_1=1\},\ h_0=\pi_0/Q(A_0=1\mid L_0,Y^{11}),\ h_1=\pi_1/Q(A_1=1\mid A_0=1,H_1,Y^{11}),\ (h_0h_1,h_1)\in\mathcal W(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\}\).

definitions.name: conditional factorization projection
definitions.construction: For \((w_0,w_1)\in\mathcal W\), define \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(L_0,Y)=\mathbb E_R[w_0\mid L_0,Y]/\mathbb E_R[w_1\mid L_0,Y]\) and \(w_0^{\mathrm{pr}}=h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(L_0,Y)w_1\).

definitions.name: joint conditional normalization system
definitions.construction: For fixed \(P,s,\eta_0,\eta_1\), define \((a_0,a_1)\) jointly by \(F_1(a_0,a_1;\eta_0,\eta_1)=0\) and \(F_0(a_0,a_1;\eta_0,\eta_1)=0\). Equivalently, for each candidate \(a_0\), take \(a_1=A_1[a_0;\eta_0,\eta_1]\) as the measurable root of the first equation and then solve \(F_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(a_0;\eta_0,\eta_1)=0\); this is a profile of a joint system, not a sequential choice of \(a_1\) before \(a_0\).

definitions.name: two-global-price conditional-root dual
definitions.construction: For \(\eta_0,\eta_1>0\), use the displayed \(u_0,\phi_0,u_1,\phi_1\), obtain \((a_0,a_1)\) from the joint conditional normalization system, and set \(\mathfrak D_s=-\{\eta_0\Sigma_0+\eta_1\Sigma_1\}/2-\mathbb E_R[a_0]-\mathbb E_R[a_1]+\mathbb E_R[\phi_1]\); on zero-price faces take the lower-semicontinuous positive-price envelope, and on a unit-budget face first impose its forced equality in the primal.

definitions.name: profiled price-residual system
definitions.construction: For \(\mathbf b=(\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\in S\) and \(\eta=(\eta_0,\eta_1)\in\mathcal U_{P,s,\mathbf b}\), obtain \((a_0,a_1)\) from the joint conditional system, set \(R_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta)=\bigl(\mathbb E_R[u_0^2u_1]-\Sigma_0,\mathbb E_R[u_1^2]-\Sigma_1\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\), designate the population root \(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b}\) by \(R_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b})=0\), and write \(J_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta)=D_{\eta}R_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\eta)\). After fixing \(\bar r\), \(\rho_{\eta}\), and \(\omega_J\), choose a common \(r\in(0,\bar r]\) satisfying \(\omega_J(r)\le\rho_{\eta}/2\); every smaller local price ball uses this derived radius. No global injectivity is imposed.

definitions.name: cross-fitted one-step endpoint process
definitions.construction: Split \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into a fixed number of folds, estimate \(\beta\) on each training complement, deterministically clip each propensity learner to \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\), evaluate the corresponding \(\Psi_s\) on its held-out fold, average the held-out scores to obtain \(\widehat v_s\), and use one common multiplier draw for the pair \((\widehat v_{+1},-\widehat v_{-1})\) over \(S\).

definitions.name: conditional-root stability and quadratic-bias handle
definitions.construction: Apply a measurable implicit-function argument to the joint operator \(\mathcal F\), using the inner profile \(A_1[a_0]\) only after fixing a candidate \(a_0\); work along positivity-preserving nuisance paths in \(\mathcal B_{\beta}^{+}(\delta)\), control clipping-set changes by the problem-specific anti-concentration bound, derive existence and localization of nuisance-perturbed roots and a local perturbation inequality for \(R_{P,s,\mathbf b}\), and telescope the orthogonal longitudinal augmentation including both propensity-floor terms to prove the second-order \(L^2(P)\) remainder. Use componentwise derivative checks on the active-clipping finite model as an early falsification test.

definitions.name: generic calibration-curve inverse functional
definitions.construction: For every nonincreasing \(g:[0,\kappa_{\max}]\to\mathbb R\), define \(T_b[g]=\inf\{\kappa\in[0,\kappa_{\max}]:g(\kappa)\le b\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). At a tied or flat crossing, \(T_b[g]\) is the left endpoint of the first crossing interval; if no crossing occurs, it equals \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: range-extended monotone band inversion
definitions.construction: Given a simultaneous band \([\ell^{\mathrm{reg}},u^{\mathrm{reg}}]\) where \(r_c(\kappa)\in S\), define \(\bar\ell(\kappa)=\operatorname{clip}_{[y_{\min},y_{\max}]}\{\ell^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\}\) and \(\bar u(\kappa)=\operatorname{clip}_{[y_{\min},y_{\max}]}\{u^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\}\) on that region, and set \(\bar\ell(\kappa)=y_{\min}\), \(\bar u(\kappa)=y_{\max}\) elsewhere. Set \(\ell^{\mathrm{mon}}(\kappa)=\sup_{t\in[\kappa,\kappa_{\max}]}\bar\ell(t)\), \(u^{\mathrm{mon}}(\kappa)=\inf_{t\in[0,\kappa]}\bar u(t)\), and \(C_b=\{T_b[g]:g\text{ is nonincreasing and }\ell^{\mathrm{mon}}\le g\le u^{\mathrm{mon}}\}\), using the tied, flat, and empty-crossing conventions in \(T_b\). Deterministic containment observation: on the simultaneous-band event, \(g_P\) is one of the admissible monotone functions between the two envelopes, so \(T_b[g_P]\in C_b\) directly by this definition.

statements.statement: For every \((w_0,w_1)\in\mathcal W(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\), \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\) is well defined and \((w_0^{\mathrm{pr}},w_1)\in\mathcal W(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\). The projected pair preserves both conditional normalizations and \(\mathbb E_R[Yw_0]\), satisfies the unambiguous product identity \(w_0^{\mathrm{pr}}=h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(L_0,Y)w_1\), and obeys \(\mathbb E_R[(w_0^{\mathrm{pr}})^2/w_1]\le\mathbb E_R[w_0^2/w_1]\).
statements.justification: This is the first changed proof step: it restores Tan's restricted early-history ratio without sacrificing the Zhang--Zhao perspective budget.
statements.gap: Neither Tan's box-constrained construction nor the one-treatment optimizer in Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 contains this weighted conditional projection.
statements.consumer: It turns any relaxed convex optimizer into a legal sequential propensity-ratio witness.

statements.statement: For every sign and positive price vector in the local domain, the Caratheodory, bracketing, and strict-monotonicity conditions yield a unique measurable solution of the joint system. Specifically, for each candidate \(a_0\), \(a_1=A_1[a_0;\eta_0,\eta_1]\) is the unique measurable root of \(F_1=0\), and the unique measurable root of \(F_0^{\mathrm{pr}}(a_0;\eta_0,\eta_1)=0\) determines the population pair \((a_0,a_1)\).
statements.justification: The measurable-root step separates population well-posedness from the genuinely open stability of roots under nuisance perturbations.
statements.gap: The one-treatment conditional root in Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 does not address a late residual that depends on the baseline multiplier through \(\phi_0\).
statements.consumer: The dual and optimized-value score receive well-defined population normalization functions without assuming any estimated root exists.

statements.statement: For every finite \(\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1\ge1\), \(\Theta(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=[L(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1),U(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)]\). The feasible perspective class is weakly compact in \(L^{4/3}(R)\times L^2(R)\). For every projected feasible pair there is a compatible law \(Q^{\mathrm{pr}}\in\mathcal M(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\) under which the original full-law ratio \(h_0\) equals \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\), \(h_1=w_1\), \(h_0h_1=h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}w_1=w_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\), and \(\mathbb E_{Q^{\mathrm{pr}}}[Y^{11}]=\mathbb E_R[Yw_0^{\mathrm{pr}}]\); hence compatible laws attain both endpoints and every intermediate value. The class is not representable by any finite Tan range bound because it permits feasible unbounded ratios.
statements.justification: Exact compatible sharpness distinguishes a sensitivity bound from a relaxation and supplies endpoint-attaining counterfactual laws.
statements.gap: Tan proves compatible sharpness for range-bounded ratios, while Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 characterizes a one-treatment second-moment optimizer; neither proves this sequential transported-perspective program.
statements.consumer: Applied investigators obtain an exact sensitivity interval for the sustained \((1,1)\) regime rather than a conservative outer bound.

statements.statement: The value \(v_s(P,\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\) equals \(\sup\mathfrak D_s\). For positive prices the jointly defined conditional roots exist measurably and are unique, the penalized optimizer is \((u_0u_1,u_1)\), and only \((\eta_0,\eta_1)\) are global. The lower-semicontinuous envelope gives the correct value when a price is zero; if \(\Sigma_t=1\), exact primal reduction precedes dual evaluation.
statements.justification: Two scalar shadow prices and conditional root equations make the infinite-dimensional sharp bound directly computable while retaining boundary correctness.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 has one global price; Tan has sequential convex representations but not the coupled quadratic perspective dual or its inactive faces.
statements.consumer: The dual supplies a stable implementation and the optimizer primitives needed for differentiation and calibration curves.

statements.statement: On the face \(\Sigma_0=1\), \(w_0=w_1\) and the signed endpoint is the infimum of \(\mathbb E_R[sYw_1]\) over \(w_1\ge\pi_1\), \(\mathbb E_R[w_1\mid H_1]=1\), and \(\mathbb E_R[w_1^2]\le\Sigma_1\). On the face \(\Sigma_1=1\), \(w_1=1\), and after factorization projection the signed endpoint is the infimum of \(\mathbb E_R[sYh_0^{\mathrm{pr}}]\) over \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\ge\pi_0\), \(\mathbb E_R[h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\mid L_0]=1\), and \(\mathbb E_R[(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}})^2]\le\Sigma_0\). Both are clipped-affine quadratic-moment programs induced directly by the present perspective model. Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 characterizes their one-treatment sensitivity-value optimizer, but its covariate-indexed roots and coefficients do not establish equivalence with either fixed-budget face here.
statements.justification: Direct face characterization prevents an invalid identification of global-budget optimizers with a comparator having covariate-indexed coefficients.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 characterizes a one-treatment sensitivity-value optimizer, not an equivalence theorem for either sequential unit-budget face.
statements.consumer: Implementations receive the exact face constraints they must solve without importing unsupported one-treatment coefficients.

statements.statement: The identities \(\mathbb E_R[(w_1-1)^2]=\mathbb E_R[w_1^2]-1\) and \(\mathbb E_R[(w_0-w_1)^2/w_1]=\mathbb E_R[w_0^2/w_1]-1\) imply that \(\Sigma_1=1\) forces \(w_1=1\), \(\Sigma_0=1\) forces \(w_0=w_1\), and \((\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=(1,1)\) gives \(L=U=\mathbb E_R[Y]\).
statements.justification: These identities prevent invalid finite-price calculations on unit-budget faces and provide the required known special-case reduction.
statements.gap: The boundary geometry is absent from the positive-price one-period formula and from sequential range-bounded analyses.
statements.consumer: Implementations can dispatch boundary calibrations exactly and avoid false optimizer certificates.

statements.statement: Under the stated primitive overlap, positivity-preserving nuisance set, problem-specific clipping anti-concentration, joint-residual neighborhood regularity, local \(C^1\) price-residual, Jacobian-modulus, pathwise score-smoothness, and nuisance-estimability conditions, can one prove that every sufficiently small nuisance perturbation admits locally unique measurable joint conditional roots in a fixed smaller neighborhood, that the population price root is the unique zero in \(\overline B(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b},r)\), and that a locally unique perturbed price root \(\widetilde\eta\) exists in a fixed smaller ball and satisfies \(\|\widetilde\eta-\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b}\|\le(2/\rho_{\eta})\sup_{\zeta\in\overline B(\eta_{P,s,\mathbf b},r)}\|R^{\widetilde\beta}_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\zeta)-R_{P,s,\mathbf b}(\zeta)\|\)? Along every admissible positivity-preserving path through \(\beta\), can one prove Neyman orthogonality of the explicit score and the exact second-order bound \(\sup_{s,\mathbf b\in S}|P\Psi_s(\widetilde\beta;\mathbf b)-v_s(P,\mathbf b)|\le C\{\sum_j\|\widetilde\beta_j-\beta_j\|_{L^2(P)}\}^2\), so that the cross-fitted held-out bias is \(O_P(\Delta_n^2)\), with separate expansions of both propensity-floor corrections?
statements.justification: This is the genuine open statistical kernel; it must derive orthogonality and optimizer stability rather than assume an estimator-side remainder.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zhao's Theorem 1 gives the one-treatment average-case influence function, Bonvini et al. give a different longitudinal recursion, and DML does not cover a joint constrained-root operator with two moving propensity floors and global prices.
statements.consumer: A positive answer licenses flexible machine learning for sharp sequential average-confounding endpoints.

statements.statement: If the conclusion in Open-ended Question 1 holds, then jointly for both signs, \(\sup_{s,(\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)\in S}|\sqrt n(\widehat v_s-v_s)-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD_s(O_i;\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)|=o_P(1)\). The endpoint pair converges in \(\ell^\infty(\{+1,-1\}\times S)\) to its Gaussian process, and a common multiplier critical value yields a simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-band for \((L,U)\) on \(S\).
statements.justification: Uniform joint inference is needed for sensitivity curves and cannot be obtained by taking a union of pointwise intervals.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zhao's Section 4.4 multiplier band is for one treatment; longitudinal sensitivity inference in Bonvini et al. targets a differently constrained endpoint.
statements.consumer: The band supports simultaneous statements about all regular calibrations and both sharp endpoints.

statements.statement: If the conclusion in Open-ended Question 1 holds, the sequential lower-endpoint process admits the simultaneous Gaussian band on \(\{\kappa:r_c(\kappa)\in S\}\). Extending this band by \([y_{\min},y_{\max}]\) and monotonizing it yields simultaneous coverage of the nonincreasing true curve \(g_P\) on the entire closed calibration ray, including zero-price, unit-budget, and other excluded faces. Consequently, the deterministic construction rule for \(C_b\) gives \(\liminf_nP(\kappa_b^\star\in C_b)\ge1-\alpha\) at unique crossings, ties, flat crossing intervals, and absent crossings. No shrinking Gaussian approximation is asserted on the excluded faces.
statements.justification: Set inversion preserves honest coverage when inverse-function asymptotics fail or a calibration ray never crosses the benchmark.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3 characterizes the sensitivity-value optimizer for their one-treatment average-case model.
He gives ``explicit representations for the sharp and conservative bounds at the population level'' under range-bounded ratios.
They ``develop efficient estimators and confidence intervals for bounds'' in three distinct MSM sensitivity models.
They ``derive the sharp partial identification bounds'' for a one-treatment odds-ratio model.
They combine orthogonal scores with \(K\)-fold sample splitting, called cross-fitting.
They construct inner and outer confidence sets by inverting simultaneous confidence intervals.
They provide bootstrap lower uniform confidence bands for one-period breakdown frontiers.
They show that the standard bootstrap generally fails without full differentiability.

tldr: Worst-case propensity-ratio caps can be driven by rare histories, while a second-moment budget measures average confounding strength. For the fixed two-decision regime \((1,1)\), the compatible mean set is characterized as an exact compact interval generated by a convex perspective program. A conditional projection defines the observed-law ratio \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\) separately from the original full-law ratio \(h_0\), restores the required early-history factorization, and supports compatible laws attaining the endpoints. The two-global-price dual uses a joint conditional normalization system and handles active, zero-price, and unit-budget faces through clipped-affine quadratic-perspective geometry. The statistical frontier is an explicit cross-fitted optimized-value score with propensity learners clipped away from zero and one and with two indispensable propensity-floor corrections. Resolving local existence and stability of nuisance-perturbed joint roots, price perturbations, Neyman orthogonality, and the second-order \(L^2(P)\) remainder yields a joint multiplier band whose deterministic range extension remains honest at tied, flat, or absent breakdown crossings.

project_justification.gap: Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3, Theorem 1, and Section 4.4 treat a one-treatment second-moment model, whereas Tan treats sequential compatibility under range-bounded ratios; neither covers the two-decision transported-perspective model and its coupled inference problem.
project_justification.niche: Sequential normalization couples an early ratio to the late ratio through a product weight and a transported perspective moment, producing a two-price optimizer and a score whose clipping floors both move with the observed law.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact compatible sharpness, attainment, boundary-correct duality, and a falsifiable route to uniform endpoint and breakdown-region inference under primitive learner and clipping conditions.

related_work: Tan's Lemma 1 supplies the full-law compatibility and constructive pasting logic, but his sensitivity ratios are bounded pointwise. Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 characterizes the one-treatment sensitivity-value optimizer, Theorem 1 supplies the average-case influence-function template, and Section 4.4 supplies the multiplier-band architecture. Their model has one treatment and a marginal second-moment restriction, whereas the present model has two decision-specific normalizations and the transported perspective moment \(\mathbb E_R[w_0^2/w_1]\). The present unit-budget faces are clipped-affine quadratic-moment programs derived from the sequential perspective class. Proposition 3 has covariate-indexed roots and coefficients and does not by itself establish equality with either fixed-budget face optimizer. Bonvini, Kennedy, Ventura, and Wasserman supply a longitudinal influence-function recursion for different sensitivity restrictions and therefore inform rather than subsume the score. Dorn, Guo, and Kallus connect sharp sensitivity optimization to efficient endpoint estimation in a one-treatment odds-ratio model. Chernozhukov et al. supply cross-fitting and orthogonal-score remainder control. Ren, Telschow, and Schwartzman supply deterministic inverse-set coverage; Masten and Poirier motivate breakdown frontiers; Fang and Santos explain why ordinary smooth bootstrap arguments cannot be imposed at ties.
technical_internal_limitation: Existence, local uniqueness, and localization of nuisance-perturbed conditional and price roots, the price perturbation bound, score orthogonality, and the uniform second-order \(L^2(P)\) held-out bias bound are not treated as established. Nuisance perturbations and foldwise propensity estimates are restricted by deterministic clipping to remain between \(\epsilon/2\) and \(1-\epsilon/2\); the resulting \(L^2(P)\) set is used only through admissible paths and is not treated as an open differentiability domain. The primitive neighborhood assumptions do not assert that perturbed roots exist, remain localized, or are inverse-Lipschitz, and they do not assert global invertibility of the profiled price-residual map. The local radius \(r\) is chosen from the Jacobian modulus and nonsingularity bound rather than imposed through a separate small-variation assumption. The Gaussian endpoint band and full-ray statistical coverage are conditional on a positive resolution of Open-ended Question 1. The early kill test perturbs every component of a finite two-baseline, two-history, three-outcome law with active clipping at both stages and compares constrained-value derivatives with score covariances, then jointly perturbs nuisances and prices. A reproducible first-order mismatch kills the inference theorem. Gaussian shrinking bands are asserted only on \(S\); zero-price and unit-budget faces receive deterministic outcome-range coverage, and learned dynamic regimes are outside scope.
honest_scope: Population sharpness, the boundary-correct two-price dual, measurable population normalization, and compatible attainment are theorem obligations. The two unit-budget faces are characterized directly as clipped-affine quadratic-moment problems and are not asserted copies of Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3 optimizer. Simultaneous-band inversion is a deterministic containment observation built into the definitions of \(T_b\) and \(C_b\), not an independent theorem contribution. The main open content is the nonparametric proof that positivity-preserving nearby nuisance inputs possess locally unique measurable joint roots, that conditional and price roots remain in their prescribed neighborhoods, that the price perturbation inequality holds, and that the explicit score is Neyman-orthogonal with the stated second-order \(L^2(P)\) remainder. The Gaussian endpoint process and full-ray statistical coverage depend on resolving this question. At \((\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=(1,1)\), the interval reduces to the observed target-path mean. No inference is claimed for a learned policy, and no shrinking Gaussian approximation is claimed on excluded faces.

seed_details.kernel: Exact compatible interval, projection-based factorization, attaining laws, two-price boundary-correct dual, and the inference rung for the same endpoint.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-period change of measure by product coordinates and prove that conditional projection lowers the perspective budget while preserving both normalizations and the objective.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Zhang and Zhao by applying their optimizer twice. Rebuttal: iteration does not enforce the early restricted-history ratio or the transported product budget, and it supplies neither common full-law attainment nor zero-price coupling.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not a bare convex program: it requires exact compatible full-law sharpness, an explicit non-LP dual, boundary reductions, and uniform inference.

seed_details.kernel: Uniform asymptotic linearity and a joint Gaussian multiplier band for the explicit sequential optimized-value score under primitive clipping and learner conditions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Establish a measurable implicit-function expansion for the joint conditional-root operator and two global prices while retaining both moving propensity-floor derivatives.
seed_details.red_team: Routine DML after writing an influence function. Rebuttal: the root operators, prices, and clipping sets are law-dependent, and ordinary cross-fitting does not yield the required uniform quadratic remainder.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a limit-law kernel, not a bare M8 label, and the held-out bias inequality is exposed as open.

seed_details.kernel: Honest full-calibration-ray confidence sets obtained from a joint endpoint band plus deterministic range extension and monotone inverse-set projection.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Define breakdown as a set-valued inverse and extend coverage over Gaussian-excluded faces before inversion.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate application of generic band inversion. Rebuttal: the statistical novelty lies in obtaining the sequential joint band and in coupling its regular region to honest full-ray coverage without extrapolating Gaussianity.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The inversion is not marketed alone; it is downstream of the new endpoint process.

seed_details.kernel: Support-function characterization of several regime means under one common full law, with necessary and sufficient simultaneous-attainment conditions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace single-regime pasting by a cross-regime gluing construction preserving all shared propensity and counterfactual-history identities.
seed_details.red_team: Coordinatewise bounds already determine every contrast. Rebuttal: coordinatewise extrema may use mutually incompatible latent laws, so they do not determine a common-law vector set.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Credible but deferred because the common-law gluing obstruction is less developed than the single-regime kernel.

seed_details.kernel: Canonical gradient and semiparametric efficiency bound for each regular sequential endpoint, with an attaining cross-fitted estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Decompose the tangent space into baseline, transition, outcome, and two propensity components and retain the floor derivatives.
seed_details.red_team: The envelope theorem makes the EIF automatic. Rebuttal: omitting either propensity-floor derivative changes optimized-value pathwise derivatives, and the coupled roots require a new tangent calculation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Kept below the joint proposal because pointwise efficiency alone does not deliver the requested sensitivity curve.

seed_details.kernel: Enumerate clipping faces on finite support and give exact algebraic primal-dual certificates, including inactive prices and unit budgets.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Resolve set-valued zero-price minimizers before solving the remaining polynomial root system.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely an implementation detail. Rebuttal: exact boundary certificates prevent demonstrably false positive-price solutions, but the objection caps the seed below field tier.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not selected because computation without the population or inference theorem is too narrow.

seed_details.kernel: An arbitrary-period recursive perspective formulation with a vector of global prices and jointly profiled conditional roots.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Prove a multi-stage conditional projection compatible with every transported perspective moment.
seed_details.red_team: Routine \(T=2\) to fixed \(T\) induction. Rebuttal: the projection may fail to commute across multiple history restrictions, but without a non-inductive obstruction the seed is not selected.

seed_details.red_team: Generic directional delta method solves this. Rebuttal: the sequential product constraint creates coupled face changes, but no verified local scaling law is yet available.

literature_map.settled: For a one-treatment second-moment ratio model, Proposition 3 gives the sensitivity-value optimizer, Theorem 1 gives the average-case influence function, and Section 4.4 gives multiplier bands.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those results concern one treatment and a marginal second-moment restriction; they do not contain the joint two-decision normalization system or the transported perspective moment \(\mathbb E_R[w_0^2/w_1]\), and Proposition 3 does not establish equality with either fixed-budget unit face here.

literature_map.settled: Tan's Lemma 1 gives necessary and sufficient normalization plus constructive compatible full laws for the primary sequential ratio model; population bounds use range constraints.
literature_map.open_boundary: Section 6 leaves specialized computation and sample sensitivity analysis open.

literature_map.settled: Bonvini et al. provide efficient estimators and confidence intervals for distinct propensity, outcome, and subset-confounding MSM models.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their time-varying propensity formulation does not impose the same Tan normalization and quadratic transported budgets.

literature_map.settled: Dorn, Guo, and Kallus derive sharp one-treatment odds-ratio bounds with efficient and robust estimation.
literature_map.open_boundary: The sequential second-moment target has two moving floors, conditional roots, and global prices.

literature_map.settled: Simultaneous bands can be inverted into inner and outer sets without transversal crossings; one-period breakdown frontiers have uniform lower bands.
literature_map.open_boundary: No located paper combines this with a sequential average-case endpoint process and deterministic coverage across nonregular budget faces.

novelty_justification: Zhang and Zhao's Proposition 3, Theorem 1, and Section 4.4 establish optimization, influence-function, and multiplier-band results for a one-treatment marginal second-moment model. Tan establishes longitudinal compatibility under range-bounded ratios. The theorem-level delta is the exact two-decision transported-perspective representation with a distinct projected ratio \(h_0^{\mathrm{pr}}\), compatible endpoint attainment, a boundary-correct two-price dual, and an explicit uniform-in-budget inference problem containing both propensity-floor corrections.
message: Completed the v5 whole-core repair and structural re-audit, including the atomic positivity-preserving pathwise score-smoothness condition.
